answers.question: What was the task?
answers.answer: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows it is in milliseconds.
quotes: The task was to rename the server timeout setting so that its name shows milliseconds.

answers.question: How did it end: what is done and what is not?
answers.answer: The rename is done in the code and in the team's own settings file with both tests passing, while the operations team's production file still uses the old name and was left untouched because changes to it go through operations.
quotes: That is done in the code and in our settings file, and both tests pass.
The operations team's production file still sets the timeout under the old name.
I left that file alone, because changes to it go through operations.

answers.question: How does the thing that changed work?
answers.answer: The code now reads only the new name and falls back to five seconds when it is missing, while the team's settings file sets three seconds under the new name.
quotes: The code now reads only the new name.
When the name is missing, it falls back to five seconds.
Our settings file gives three seconds under the new name.

answers.question: What is the problem, and what causes it?
answers.answer: After the release production will wait three seconds instead of ten, because the production file sets ten seconds under the old name, which the code no longer reads, so the three seconds from the team's file apply.
quotes: The code no longer reads that name, so after the release production waits three seconds instead of ten.
The operations file sets ten seconds under the old name.
So production gets our three seconds.

answers.question: What is not verified?
answers.answer: The tests do not read the production file, so the production behaviour is not covered by them.
quotes: They do not read the production file.

answers.question: What do I have to decide, and what does each option give and cost?
answers.answer: The reader decides between operations renaming their line before the release (one name everywhere and nothing to clean up, but the release waits for operations) and the code also reading the old name with priority while it is set (the release can go now and production keeps ten seconds, but two names live in the code until operations rename and the old one is removed), with the author recommending asking operations first.
quotes: You decide whether operations rename their line first, or the code keeps reading the old name for a while.
I would ask operations first: it is one line for them, and nothing is left to remove later.
Do you ask operations to rename their line, or do I make the code read the old name too?
